question: A company offers a buy 2 get 1 free scheme on pens priced at ₹10 each. What is the effective discount percentage?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For any Buy X Get Y Free scheme, the discount percentage is always calculated on the total number of items.

Discount % = [Free Items ÷ Total Items] × 100

⇒ Discount % = [1 ÷ (2 + 1)] × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 3) × 100 = 33¹/₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 33¹/₃%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked price of 1 pen = ₹10

Scheme: Buy 2 get 1 free

**Formula Used:**

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total number of pens received = 2 (bought) + 1 (free) = 3

⇒ Total Marked Price (MP) of 3 pens = 3 × 10 = ₹30

⇒ Total Selling Price (SP) for the customer (paying only for 2 pens) = 2 × 10 = ₹20

⇒ Discount amount = MP − SP = 30 − 20 = ₹10

⇒ Discount % = (10 ÷ 30) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 100 ÷ 3 = 33¹/₃%

**∴ The correct answer is 33¹/₃%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Buy X Get Y Free Rule

The effective discount is always calculated on the total number of items taken out of the shop. Effective Discount % = [Y ÷ (X + Y)] × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP), not the Cost Price (CP). Therefore, Selling Price = Marked Price × [(100 − Discount %) ÷ 100].

Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts of a% and b% are offered, the equivalent single discount percentage is [a + b − (a × b ÷ 100)]%.
